title: ESC swallow latch bypassed by drag-release click-select
detail: ESC deselect sets press_swallowed and claims the in-flight click's release 'must not re-select', but never clears drag.active, and the drag-release click-select checks only release_ui_hit — no press_swallowed gate. Node press, ESC, release-without-move re-selects what ESC deselected.
recommended_fix: Gate the drag-release click-select on !press_swallowed (matching the plain-release branch), or clear drag.active in the ESC deselect branch.

title: Chord handling contradicts PR interaction map (no swallow)
detail: PR interaction map: the chord and other interruptions 'all swallow that gesture's release so it cannot re-select'. Code sets press_swallowed = false and its comment anticipates click-select firing ('if any'). Release within 6px click-selects — contract and code contradict.
recommended_fix: Make both agree: set press_swallowed = true for the chord, or correct the PR body to say the chord re-anchors and permits click-select.

title: Off-by-one tick labels in new .dem header comments
evidence:
+# representative (pipe 1) at t23. At 1150ms (tick 24) the NON-representative
+# At 2000ms (tick 41) router 3 is DEMOLISHED: the core applies the atomic
+# (t29) = the packet delivered on the full net; 2100ms (t42) = POST-batch,
detail: At 20Hz the files' own labels make 1100ms=t22, 1300ms=t26, 2100ms=t42. So 1150ms is tick 23 (labeled 24) and 2000ms is tick 40 (labeled 41) — both headers off by one.
recommended_fix: Correct the comment labels (tick 23 / tick 40) or document the offset convention.

title: popover_rect small-window clamps contradict 'fully inside' claim
evidence:
+	if y < 8 { y = 8 }
+	// overflow a window smaller than the panel (the app is resizable)
+		y = f32(v.win_h) - TRAY_CLEAR - h
+	x = min(x, f32(v.win_w) - POPOVER_W - 8)
+	y = min(y, f32(v.win_h) - h - 8)
+// window; clamped into the viewport, ABOVE the tray band, and fully inside a
detail: Final min() clamps run after the x<8/y<8 guards and can push x/y negative when win_w < POPOVER_W+8 or win_h < h+TRAY_CLEAR — contradicting the comment's 'clamped into the viewport... fully inside a small window' claim.
recommended_fix: Re-apply the 8px guards after the final min clamps, or clamp to zero.

title: Popover can render under the HUD (draw order + top clamp)
detail: Popover draws before draw_hud, so the HUD paints over it; popover_rect permits y=8 top-left, where the file's own comment puts the QoS readout. A top-clamped popover's demolish button can sit hidden under the HUD yet remain hit-testable.
recommended_fix: Draw the popover after draw_hud, or clamp the popover below the HUD readout band.
